subject: science
title: US Middle School Science - Ecosystems and Food Webs
subtitle: Reading comprehension passages on ecosystems and food webs.
description: Reading pack for ecosystem concepts, food webs, biodiversity, and human impacts. Students practise fact retrieval, inference, data-based reasoning, and scientific explanation.

data.sourcePassage: An ecosystem is a connected system made of living and nonliving parts. In a pond ecosystem, fish, frogs, algae, insects, bacteria, water, sunlight, mud, oxygen, and temperature all interact. Scientists describe living or once-living parts as biotic factors and nonliving parts as abiotic factors. The parts do not act alone. A plant uses sunlight, water, carbon dioxide, and minerals to grow. A rabbit may eat the plant, and a fox may eat the rabbit. Fungi and bacteria break down dead plants, dead animals, and waste, returning matter to soil and water.

questions.question: What is an ecosystem?
options: A system of living and nonliving parts interacting
Only the animals in one place
A single organism and its food
questions.modelAnswer: An ecosystem is a system of living and nonliving parts interacting in an area.

questions.question: Which example from the passage is an abiotic factor?
questions.modelAnswer: Sunlight is an abiotic factor because it is nonliving.

questions.question: Why does the passage say ecosystem parts do not act alone?
questions.modelAnswer: The parts affect one another, such as plants using abiotic resources, animals eating plants, and decomposers returning matter to soil and water.

questions.question: How do fungi and bacteria support the ecosystem described?
questions.modelAnswer: They decompose dead organisms and waste, returning matter and nutrients to soil and water.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the system idea in the passage?
options: Living and nonliving parts interact and changes can affect other parts
Abiotic factors are separate from living things
Food chains do not involve nonliving factors
questions.modelAnswer: Living and nonliving parts interact, so one change can affect other parts of the ecosystem.

data.sourcePassage: Most ecosystems begin with energy from the Sun. Producers such as plants and algae capture sunlight energy through photosynthesis. They use carbon dioxide and water to make sugar and oxygen. Consumers gain energy when they eat producers or other consumers, but energy transfer is not perfect. Organisms use energy for movement, growth, body heat, repair, reproduction, and other life processes, and much energy is released as heat. Because energy is lost at each transfer, food chains usually have only a few levels. Matter is different: atoms such as carbon, oxygen, nitrogen, water, and minerals cycle between living things, air, soil, and water.

questions.question: What process do producers use to capture sunlight energy?
questions.modelAnswer: Producers use photosynthesis.

questions.question: Why do food chains usually have only a few levels?
options: All organisms are the same size
Energy is lost or used at each transfer
questions.modelAnswer: Food chains are usually short because energy is used and released as heat at each transfer.

questions.question: Explain the difference between energy flow and matter cycling.
questions.modelAnswer: Energy flows through ecosystems and is eventually released as heat, while matter cycles through organisms, air, soil, and water.

questions.question: Use the passage to explain why producers form the base of most food webs.
questions.modelAnswer: Producers capture sunlight and make sugar, bringing usable energy into the food web for consumers.

questions.question: Which claim is best supported by the passage?
options: Energy and matter both cycle forever in the same way
Energy becomes less available at higher feeding levels
questions.modelAnswer: Energy becomes less available at higher feeding levels because organisms use energy and release heat at each transfer.

data.sourcePassage: A food chain shows one possible path of energy flow, such as grass to grasshopper to frog to snake to hawk. A food web is more realistic because most organisms eat more than one kind of food and many are eaten by more than one predator. Food webs help scientists predict changes. In a meadow, hawks may eat snakes, birds, and mice. Snakes may eat frogs and mice. Frogs may eat grasshoppers, and grasshoppers eat grass. If a disease reduces the frog population, grasshoppers may face less predation. Snakes may have less frog prey and may eat more mice instead. Effects can spread through the web.

questions.question: What does a food chain show?
questions.modelAnswer: A food chain shows one possible path of energy flow.

questions.question: Why is a food web more realistic than a food chain?
options: It shows many connected feeding relationships
questions.modelAnswer: A food web is more realistic because it shows many connected feeding relationships.

questions.question: What might happen to grasshoppers if disease reduces the frog population?
questions.modelAnswer: Grasshoppers may increase because fewer frogs are available to eat them.

questions.question: How might snakes respond if frogs decrease?
questions.modelAnswer: Snakes may have less frog prey and may switch to eating more mice if available.

questions.question: Why does this scenario show that ecosystems are systems?
questions.modelAnswer: A change in one population can affect other populations through feeding relationships, so the parts are connected.

data.sourcePassage: Biodiversity means the variety of life in an ecosystem. It includes species variety, genetic variety within species, and variety of habitats. An ecosystem with high biodiversity often has more possible food sources and more ways to recover after change. For example, if one plant species decreases during a drought, herbivores may be able to eat other plants. In a low-biodiversity ecosystem, many consumers may depend on the same food source, so the loss of one species can cause a larger disruption. High biodiversity does not make an ecosystem impossible to damage, but it can improve resilience.

questions.question: What does biodiversity mean?
options: The variety of living things in an ecosystem
The amount of sunlight in a habitat
The number of rocks in soil
questions.modelAnswer: Biodiversity means the variety of living things in an ecosystem.

questions.question: Which ecosystem would likely have greater biodiversity?
options: A field with one crop species
A forest with many plants, animals, fungi, and bacteria
A parking lot with no plants
A jar with one algae species
questions.modelAnswer: A forest with many plants, animals, fungi, and bacteria would likely have greater biodiversity.

questions.question: How can biodiversity help herbivores during a drought?
questions.modelAnswer: If one plant species decreases, herbivores may have other plant species available as alternative food sources.

questions.question: Why can a low-biodiversity ecosystem be more vulnerable to change?
questions.modelAnswer: Many organisms may depend on the same species or food source, so one loss can disrupt more of the food web.

questions.question: Does high biodiversity mean an ecosystem cannot be damaged? Explain.
questions.modelAnswer: No. Pollution, habitat destruction, invasive species, climate change, and overharvesting can still harm ecosystems, but biodiversity can improve resilience.

data.sourcePassage: Fertilizers from lawns and farms can wash into lakes after rain. Fertilizers often contain nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus. Extra nutrients can cause algae to grow quickly, forming an algal bloom. At first, more algae may seem helpful because algae are producers. However, when large amounts of algae die, decomposers break them down. Decomposers use dissolved oxygen in the water during this process. If oxygen levels become too low, fish and other aquatic animals may die. This sequence shows how one human activity can affect producers, decomposers, oxygen levels, and consumers.

questions.question: What can wash fertilizer into lakes?
questions.modelAnswer: Rain and runoff can wash fertilizer into lakes.

questions.question: Which nutrients in fertilizer are named in the passage?
questions.modelAnswer: The passage names nitrogen and phosphorus.

questions.question: Why can an algal bloom lead to low dissolved oxygen?
questions.modelAnswer: When many algae die, decomposers break them down and use dissolved oxygen in the water.

questions.question: Why might fish die after an algal bloom?
questions.modelAnswer: Fish may die because decomposers use up dissolved oxygen, leaving too little oxygen for aquatic animals to survive.

questions.question: Explain why lake pollution is an ecosystem problem rather than only a water problem.
questions.modelAnswer: The added nutrients affect algae, decomposers, dissolved oxygen, fish, and other consumers, so many connected parts of the ecosystem change.
